derivation: A job's timeout-minutes is the larger of floor_minutes and ceil((bound_s + load_factor * measured_s) / 60), where bound_s is the budget of the slowest tier its pytest commands select (tier_budgets.json; 0 for a job without pytest): a hang costs one test's budget before pytest-timeout ends the process, on top of a run slowed by load. measured_s is the job's duration in the green run 42579214662 at ef52fd13; pr-models was skipped there, so it is 0 and the floor applies. load_factor 2 doubles the measured run for a loaded runner. floor_minutes 5 covers a runner that is slow to start on a job of a few seconds.
